items.title: Location, Extent, Regions & Relief
items.body:
**In one line:** This note fixes where Andhra Pradesh (AP) sits on the map, how big it is, how many districts it now has, and the three kinds of land it is made of.

**Why it is asked:** APPSC loves one-mark facts here — area rank, number of districts, the highest peak — and these facts anchor almost every other Geography answer about AP.

## The story

In **2014** the old Andhra Pradesh was split into two states: **Telangana** was carved out, and the remaining part is today's AP. Because of that split, present-day AP sits on India's **south-east coast**, with the **Bay of Bengal** to its east.

By size it covers about **1,62,970 sq km**. After Jammu & Kashmir became a Union Territory in 2019, AP is now the **7th largest** state by area, and the **10th** by population (about 4.09% of India in the 2011 Census).

The number of districts has grown in steps. It was **13** for decades, rose to **26** on **4 April 2022**, and then to **28** on **31 December 2025** when **Polavaram** and **Markapuram** districts were added. A proposed **Madanapalle** district was never created — Madanapalle is only the headquarters town of Annamayya district.

If you look at AP from the sea moving inland, the land changes in three clear belts, and this is its **physiography** (the shape of its surface).

## Picture it

| Belt (west to east) | What it is like |
|---|---|
| Rayalaseema plateau | Dry, semi-arid interior on the edge of the Deccan |
| Eastern Ghats | Broken, low hill ranges (Nallamala, Papikonda, Seshachalam, Erramala) |
| Coastal plains | Flat, fertile east-coast land with the Godavari and Krishna deltas |

The highest point is **Arma Konda (about 1,680 m)** in Alluri Sitharama Raju district — it is also the tallest peak in the whole Eastern Ghats.

**AP at a glance (after the 2014 bifurcation)**

| Point | Fact |
|---|---|
| Neighbours | shares borders with Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu; the Bay of Bengal lies to the east |
| Coastline | about 974 km — the longest of any state on India's east coast |
| Area | about 1.63 lakh sq km — India's 7th-largest state |
| Population (Census 2011) | about 4.94 crore, about 4.08% of India — the 10th most populous state |
| Density | about 304 persons per sq km — below the national average of 382 |

**The three regions and their districts**
- **Coastal Andhra (Kostha)** — the deltaic coastal belt of the Godavari and Krishna.
- **Uttarandhra (North Coastal)** — Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam and the Visakhapatnam belt.
- **Rayalaseema** — the semi-arid interior plateau (not coastal); includes Kurnool, Nandyal, Kadapa, Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, Annamayya and Chittoor.

## Terms explained

- **Bifurcation** — the 2014 splitting of one state into two (AP and Telangana).
- **Physiography** — the natural shape of the land surface (plains, hills, plateau).
- **Plateau** — a raised, flat-topped area of land; Rayalaseema sits on the Deccan plateau's margin.
- **Delta** — the fan of fertile land a river builds where it meets the sea.
- **Rayalaseema and Coastal Andhra** — AP's two broad regions; the far-north coast (Srikakulam-Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam), called Uttarandhra, is often treated as a third sub-region.

## Don't confuse

- **Districts 26 versus 28** — older books and the 2024-25 state survey still print 26; the correct current figure is **28** (since 31 Dec 2025).
- **Arma Konda is NOT Mahendragiri** — Mahendragiri is a high Eastern Ghats peak but lies on the Odisha side and is lower.
- **7th not 8th** — AP was the 8th largest state only before 2019, when J&K was still a state.

## Remember it

Count the districts up: **13, then double to 26, then plus 2 (Polavaram and Markapuram) to 28.**

## TL;DR

- AP lies on India's south-east (Bay of Bengal) coast; area about 1,62,970 sq km; 7th largest state, 10th by population.
- Districts grew 13 to 26 (4 Apr 2022) to 28 (31 Dec 2025, Polavaram and Markapuram); Madanapalle is only a headquarters.
- Three belts west to east: Rayalaseema plateau, Eastern Ghats, coastal plains.
- Highest point: Arma Konda (about 1,680 m), the tallest peak of the Eastern Ghats.
keyPoints: AP lies on India's south-east (Bay of Bengal) coast; about 1,62,970 sq km; 7th largest state and 10th by population.
Two regions (Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema); the north-coastal Srikakulam-Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam belt is a distinct sub-region.
Districts: 13 to 26 (4 April 2022) to 28 with Polavaram and Markapuram (31 December 2025); the 2024-25 survey still shows 26.
Three physiographic belts west to east: Rayalaseema plateau, Eastern Ghats, coastal plains.
Arma Konda (about 1,680 m), in Alluri Sitharama Raju district, is AP's highest point and the tallest Eastern Ghats peak.

items.title: Coastline & Ports
items.body:
**In one line:** AP has a long sea edge on the Bay of Bengal, and this coastline is both a money-maker (ports, fishing) and the reason the state is so exposed to cyclones.

**Why it is asked:** The '974 km' figure and the name of AP's only major port (Visakhapatnam) are classic one-mark questions; the coast also links to economy and disaster-management answers.

## The story

A **coastline** is simply the length of the boundary where the land meets the sea. AP's coastline runs about **974 km** along the Bay of Bengal — the **longest of any state on India's east coast**.

The shape of this coast changes as you move along it. In the centre it is low and flat, built up by the mud the **Godavari and Krishna** rivers drop as they reach the sea. In the north, around **Visakhapatnam**, it is rockier, which is why a deep natural harbour could form there.

That natural harbour makes **Visakhapatnam** AP's only **major port** (a 'major' port is one run under the central government). Alongside it, several **non-major ports** — **Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada and Machilipatnam** — handle cargo, fishing boats and industry. Because the coast is so long, AP is also a national leader in **fishing and shrimp farming (aquaculture)**, much of it exported.

## Picture it

| Port | Type |
|---|---|
| Visakhapatnam | Major port (central government); deep natural harbour |
| Krishnapatnam | Non-major port |
| Gangavaram | Non-major port |
| Kakinada | Non-major port |
| Machilipatnam | Non-major port |

## Terms explained

- **Coastline** — the length of the shore where land meets the sea.
- **Major port** — a large port administered by the central government; AP has exactly one (Visakhapatnam).
- **Harbour** — a sheltered stretch of water where ships can anchor safely.
- **Aquaculture** — farming fish or shrimp in ponds or coastal waters, rather than catching them wild.

## Don't confuse

- **Longest on the east coast, not in all India** — Gujarat has India's longest coastline overall; AP's 974 km is the longest on the eastern side.
- **Major versus non-major port** — only Visakhapatnam is 'major'; Kakinada, Krishnapatnam and the rest are non-major, even though they are busy.

## Remember it

'**974** — nine, seven, four' is AP's east-coast score; and its one big port starts with the same sound as the state's biggest city, **V**isakhapatnam.

## TL;DR

- AP's coastline is about 974 km, the longest on India's east coast.
- Visakhapatnam is AP's only major (central-government) port, built on a natural harbour.
- Non-major ports: Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada, Machilipatnam.
- The long coast powers fishing and shrimp aquaculture but also exposes AP to Bay of Bengal cyclones.
keyPoints: AP coastline is about 974 km, the longest on India's east coast.
Visakhapatnam is AP's only major (central-government) port, a deep natural harbour.
Non-major ports: Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada, Machilipatnam.
The coast supports fishing and shrimp aquaculture but is highly cyclone-prone.

items.title: Rivers, River-sharing & Irrigation Projects
items.body:
**In one line:** AP's rivers all flow east into the Bay of Bengal, feed its deltas, and are tapped by big dams and lift schemes — most famously Polavaram on the Godavari.

**Why it is asked:** Matching a reservoir to its river (Nagarjuna Sagar to Krishna, Somasila to Pennar, Polavaram to Godavari) is a very common APPSC match-the-following item.

## The story

AP has about **40 rivers** of all sizes, and **15 of them are inter-state** (they are shared with neighbouring states). Every important river flows **eastward into the Bay of Bengal**.

The two giants are the **Godavari** and the **Krishna**. The **Godavari** is the largest river of peninsular India and is nicknamed the **'Dakshina Ganga'** (the Ganga of the South); it builds the lush Konaseema delta. The **Krishna** builds its own delta near Machilipatnam. In the dry south, the **Pennar (Penna)** waters Rayalaseema and Nellore, while in the far north the **Vamsadhara and Nagavali** (shared with Odisha) drain the Srikakulam-Vizianagaram belt.

Because rain is uneven, AP stores and moves river water using **irrigation projects**. A dam creates a **reservoir** (a man-made lake) whose water is let out through canals. The flagship is **Polavaram** on the Godavari, which the centre has made a **National Project**. On the Krishna sit **Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam**; on the Pennar sits **Somasila**. A **lift scheme** called **Handri-Neeva** even pumps Krishna water uphill into drought-hit Rayalaseema.

## Picture it

| Reservoir / project | River | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Polavaram | Godavari | National Project; AP's flagship |
| Nagarjuna Sagar | Krishna | Large multipurpose reservoir |
| Srisailam | Krishna | Hydro-power and irrigation |
| Somasila | Pennar | Serves Nellore / Rayalaseema |
| Handri-Neeva (lift) | Krishna water | Pumped to Rayalaseema |

## Terms explained

- **Inter-state river** — a river shared by more than one state, so its water is divided by agreements or tribunals.
- **Reservoir** — the lake of water held back by a dam.
- **National Project** — a scheme the central government funds and supervises because of its national importance; Polavaram is one.
- **Lift scheme** — a project that pumps water uphill, against gravity, to reach dry higher land.
- **Dakshina Ganga** — 'Ganga of the South', the Godavari's nickname.

## Don't confuse

- **Polavaram is on the Godavari, not the Krishna.** The Krishna carries Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam.
- **Somasila is on the Pennar**, not the Godavari or Krishna.
- **Vamsadhara/Nagavali are shared with Odisha**, while the Krishna and Pennar are shared with Karnataka.

## Remember it

Delta duo = **Godavari + Krishna**; Rayalaseema's lifeline = **Handri-Neeva**.

## TL;DR

- About 40 rivers (15 inter-state); all major rivers drain east into the Bay of Bengal.
- Godavari (largest peninsular river, 'Dakshina Ganga') and Krishna build AP's deltas.
- Polavaram is a National Project on the Godavari; Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam are on the Krishna; Somasila is on the Pennar.
- Handri-Neeva lifts Krishna water to drought-prone Rayalaseema.
keyPoints: AP has about 40 rivers (15 inter-state); all major rivers drain east into the Bay of Bengal.
Godavari (largest peninsular river, 'Dakshina Ganga') is shared with Maharashtra, Odisha, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh and MP.
Krishna is shared with Maharashtra and Karnataka; Pennar with Karnataka; Vamsadhara and Nagavali with Odisha.
Polavaram is a National Project on the Godavari; Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam are on the Krishna; Somasila on the Pennar.
Handri-Neeva lifts Krishna water to Rayalaseema.

items.title: Climate, Agro-climatic Zones, Soils & Land Use
items.body:
**In one line:** AP's weather splits into a wet, cyclone-hit coast and a dry, drought-prone interior; its soils and land use follow the same split, with crop-growing land taking the biggest share.

**Why it is asked:** The 'six agro-climatic zones', the name of the drought zone, and 'which soil in the delta' are frequent one-mark questions.

## The story

AP's **climate** is broadly **tropical** (hot). But it is not the same everywhere. The **coast** is hot, humid and among India's **most cyclone-prone** areas, because Bay of Bengal storms hit it. **Rayalaseema**, especially **Anantapuramu**, is **semi-arid and drought-prone** — one of the driest tracts in India.

Most rain comes from the **south-west monsoon** (June to September). Unusually, the **south coast** also gets useful rain from the **north-east (retreating) monsoon** (October to December), when winds reverse and blow back out over the sea.

To plan farming, AP is divided into **six agro-climatic zones** — areas grouped by their climate and soil: **North Coastal, Godavari, Krishna, Southern, Scarce Rainfall** (Kurnool and Anantapuramu) and a distinct **High Altitude & Tribal Areas** zone (the Eastern Ghats agency belt). The dry Kurnool and Anantapuramu tract is the **Scarce Rainfall Zone**.

**Soil** is the loose top layer plants grow in. The rich **deltaic alluvial** soil of the Godavari-Krishna deltas grows paddy; **black cotton (regur)** soil covers the Deccan and Rayalaseema; **red loamy and sandy** soils fill the interior.

Finally, **land use** describes how the state's total area is used. Crop land (**net area sown**) takes the single biggest share.

## Picture it

| Land-use category (2023-24) | Share |
|---|---|
| Net area sown | about 30.4% |
| Recorded forest | about 22.63% |
| Current fallows | about 14.9% |
| Non-agricultural use | about 12.84% |
| Barren / uncultivable | about 8.19% |

## Terms explained

- **Tropical climate** — a hot climate with no true cold season.
- **Semi-arid** — dry, with low and unreliable rainfall, but not a full desert.
- **Agro-climatic zone** — a region grouped by its climate and soil for farm planning; AP has six.
- **Alluvial soil** — fertile soil made of silt a river deposits.
- **Net area sown** — the land actually under crops in a year (the biggest land use in AP).
- **Current fallow** — farm land left unsown for a season to recover.

**Which soil, where**

| Soil | Where in AP |
|---|---|
| Red loamy / sandy | the most widespread soil, especially in Rayalaseema and the interior |
| Black cotton (regur) | the Krishna–Guntur belt and parts of Rayalaseema (Kurnool) |
| Deltaic alluvial | the Godavari–Krishna deltas (paddy) |
| Laterite | small patches on the Eastern Ghats uplands |
| Coastal sandy / saline | the narrow strip along the sea |

## Don't confuse

- **South-west versus north-east monsoon** — the south-west (June-September) gives most of AP's rain; the north-east (October-December) adds extra rain mainly on the south coast.
- **Six zones, not five or seven** — the drought one is the Scarce Rainfall Zone (Kurnool + Anantapuramu).

## Remember it

Coast = **wet and stormy**; Rayalaseema = **dry and thirsty**; crop land wins the land-use share.

## TL;DR

- Climate is tropical: a cyclone-prone humid coast versus a semi-arid, drought-prone Rayalaseema (Anantapuramu is driest).
- Most rain is from the south-west monsoon; the south coast also gains north-east (retreating) monsoon rain.
- Six agro-climatic zones; the Scarce Rainfall Zone is Kurnool + Anantapuramu.
- Main soils: deltaic alluvial, black cotton (regur) and red loamy/sandy; net area sown (about 30.4%) is the largest land use.
keyPoints: AP climate is tropical: cyclone-prone humid coast versus semi-arid, drought-prone Rayalaseema (Anantapuramu driest).
South coastal districts also gain rain from the north-east (retreating) monsoon.
Six agro-climatic zones; the Scarce Rainfall zone is Kurnool + Anantapuramu.
Main soils: deltaic/coastal alluvial, black cotton (regur) and red loamy/sandy.
Land use (2023-24): net sown area about 30.4% (largest); recorded forest about 22.63%; total area about 162.97 lakh ha.
items.source: AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 (agro-climatic zones, soils, land use); IMD AP climate profile

items.title: Minerals & Forests (ISFR 2023)
items.body:
**In one line:** AP is so rich in minerals it is nicknamed 'Ratna Garbha', and it also holds important forests, including India's famous second-largest mangroves.

**Why it is asked:** Matching a mineral to its place (barytes-Mangampeta, uranium-Thummalapalli, granite-Chimakurthy) and the ISFR forest figures are standard APPSC items.

## The story

A **mineral** is a useful natural substance dug from the earth. AP has so many that it is called **'Ratna Garbha'** — 'womb of gems'. Its best-known deposits are the **barytes** of **Mangampeta** (YSR Kadapa), among the **largest in the world**; the **uranium** of **Thummalapalli**; and the prized **black granite** of **Chimakurthy** (Prakasam). The long coast adds **heavy mineral beach sands** (such as ilmenite and monazite).

Forests are measured in two different ways, and students often mix them up. **Forest cover** is what satellites actually see as green canopy. **Recorded (notified) forest area** is the land the government has officially marked as forest on paper — it is usually larger, because some marked land has lost its trees.

By the **India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2023**, AP's **forest cover is 30,084.96 sq km, about 18.46%** of the state, while its **recorded forest area is 37,221.11 sq km, about 22.84%**. **Alluri Sitharama Raju** has the most forest; **Guntur** among the least. AP's **mangroves** (salt-tolerant coastal trees) in the Godavari and Krishna estuaries form India's **second-largest** mangrove stretch after the Sundarbans, protected mainly at **Coringa**.

## Picture it

| Place | Mineral |
|---|---|
| Mangampeta (YSR Kadapa) | Barytes (among world's largest) |
| Thummalapalli (YSR Kadapa) | Uranium |
| Chimakurthy (Prakasam) | Black granite |
| North-coast beaches | Heavy mineral sands |

**Limestone** for the cement industry occurs in the **Kadapa and Kurnool basins**; the Srikakulam-Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam coast holds heavy-mineral beach sands (ilmenite, garnet and monazite, the last being a source of thorium).

## Terms explained

- **Mineral** — a useful natural material mined from the ground.
- **Ratna Garbha** — 'womb of gems', AP's nickname for its mineral wealth.
- **Barytes** — a heavy white mineral used in oil-drilling fluids, paint and chemicals.
- **Forest cover** — tree canopy actually seen by satellite.
- **Recorded (notified) forest area** — land legally marked as forest on paper (usually larger than cover).
- **Mangrove** — salt-tolerant trees that grow where river estuaries meet the sea.

**Mica — the Nellore belt**
The **Nellore** (Gudur–Nellore) belt is AP's mica country and one of India's main mica belts — so in a place-to-mineral match, Nellore pairs with **mica**.

## Don't confuse

- **Forest cover (18.46%) is NOT the same as recorded forest area (22.84%)** — one is seen by satellite, the other is a legal paper figure.
- **Barytes is Mangampeta; uranium is Thummalapalli** — do not swap them, even though both are in Kadapa.

## Remember it

Kadapa's twin treasures = **Barytes (Mangampeta) + Uranium (Thummalapalli)**; satellite cover (18.46%) is less than the paper figure (22.84%).

## TL;DR

- AP = 'Ratna Garbha'; minerals include barytes, uranium, black granite, beach sands, limestone, iron ore and diamonds.
- Mangampeta (Kadapa) barytes is among the world's largest; uranium at Thummalapalli; black granite at Chimakurthy.
- ISFR 2023: forest cover 18.46% (30,084.96 sq km) versus recorded forest area 22.84% (37,221.11 sq km).
- AP has India's second-largest mangroves (Godavari and Krishna estuaries; Coringa is the main sanctuary).
keyPoints: AP = 'Ratna Garbha'; minerals include barytes, oil/gas, beach sands, limestone, iron ore, uranium, granite and diamonds.
Mangampeta (YSR Kadapa) is among the world's largest barytes deposits; uranium at Thummalapalli; black granite at Chimakurthy.
ISFR 2023: forest cover 18.46% (30,084.96 sq km) versus recorded/notified forest area 22.84% (37,221.11 sq km) — different concepts.
Alluri Sitharama Raju has AP's largest forest cover; Guntur the least.
AP has India's second-largest mangroves in the Godavari and Krishna estuaries (Coringa).

items.title: Protected Areas, Wetlands, Biodiversity & Hazards
items.body:
**In one line:** AP protects its wildlife through a small set of flagship reserves and wetlands, while its coast and interior face sharp natural hazards — cyclones and floods on one side, drought on the other.

**Why it is asked:** 'NSTR is a tiger reserve', 'Seshachalam is the biosphere reserve', 'Kolleru is the Ramsar site' and 'Hudhud 2014 hit Visakhapatnam' are repeat APPSC facts.

## The story

A **protected area** is land set aside by law to save wildlife. Present-day AP has a compact network: **one Tiger Reserve** — **Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam (NSTR)**, about 3,727 sq km and among India's largest, in the Nallamala hills where the **Chenchu**, a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG), inhabit the Nallamala forests within the reserve; **one Elephant Reserve** — **Rayala (Koundinya)** in Chittoor; **one Biosphere Reserve** — **Seshachalam**, home of the endemic **Red Sanders** tree; plus **three National Parks** (including **Sri Venkateswara** and **Papikonda**) and **13 Wildlife Sanctuaries**.

AP's **wetlands** matter too. **Kolleru Lake**, lying between the Krishna and Godavari deltas, is a large **freshwater** lake and AP's only **Ramsar site** (a wetland of international importance). **Pulicat** is a **brackish** (part-salty) lagoon shared with Tamil Nadu; **Rollapadu** in Kurnool protects the **Great Indian Bustard**.

A **hazard** is a natural event that can cause disaster. The AP coast is among India's **most cyclone-prone**: **Cyclone Hudhud (2014)** devastated Visakhapatnam. The Godavari and Krishna bring **floods** and **storm surges**, and the shore suffers **erosion**. In contrast, **Rayalaseema** repeatedly faces **drought**.

## Picture it

| Protected area | Type |
|---|---|
| Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam (NSTR) | Tiger Reserve (among India's largest) |
| Seshachalam | Biosphere Reserve (Red Sanders) |
| Koundinya (Rayala) | Elephant Reserve |
| Kolleru | Ramsar freshwater lake |
| Pulicat | Brackish lagoon (shared with Tamil Nadu) |

## Terms explained

- **Protected area** — land legally set aside to conserve wildlife.
- **Tiger / Elephant / Biosphere Reserve** — different categories of protected land for specific species or whole ecosystems.
- **Ramsar site** — a wetland listed as internationally important; Kolleru is AP's only one.
- **Brackish** — water that is a mix of fresh and salty, as in a coastal lagoon.
- **Hazard** — a natural event (cyclone, flood, drought) that can cause harm.

## Don't confuse

- **NSTR is a Tiger Reserve; Seshachalam is the Biosphere Reserve** — do not swap them.
- **Kolleru is freshwater and Ramsar-listed; Pulicat is brackish and NOT Ramsar-listed.**
- **The old '6 national parks / 21 sanctuaries' count was for undivided AP** and is outdated.

## Remember it

AP's conservation 'ones': **1 tiger reserve (NSTR), 1 elephant reserve, 1 biosphere reserve, 1 Ramsar site (Kolleru).**

## TL;DR

- Present-day AP: 1 Tiger Reserve (NSTR), 1 Elephant Reserve (Rayala/Koundinya), 1 Biosphere Reserve (Seshachalam), 3 National Parks, 13 Sanctuaries.
- Kolleru (freshwater, Ramsar) lies between the Krishna and Godavari deltas; Pulicat is a brackish lagoon shared with Tamil Nadu.
- Rollapadu (Kurnool) conserves the Great Indian Bustard; Coringa protects Godavari-estuary mangroves.
- The coast is highly cyclone-prone (Hudhud 2014 hit Visakhapatnam); floods, storm surge and erosion threaten it, while Rayalaseema faces drought.
keyPoints: Present-day AP: 1 Tiger Reserve (NSTR), 1 Elephant Reserve (Rayala/Koundinya), 1 Biosphere Reserve (Seshachalam), 3 National Parks, 13 Sanctuaries.
Kolleru (freshwater, Ramsar) lies between the Krishna and Godavari deltas; Pulicat is a brackish lagoon shared with Tamil Nadu.
Rollapadu (Kurnool) conserves the Great Indian Bustard; Coringa protects Godavari-estuary mangroves.
AP is in the Deccan Bio-Geographic Zone; endemic Red Sanders; fauna include Golden Gecko, Indian Bison, Great Indian Bustard.
The AP coast is highly cyclone-prone (Hudhud 2014 hit Visakhapatnam); floods, storm surge, coastal erosion and Rayalaseema drought are key hazards.
items.source: AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25; AP Protected Areas & Wildlife (2011); disaster records

items.title: Flora, Fauna, Forests & Sanctuaries of Andhra Pradesh
items.body:
**In one line:** AP's forests are mostly dry deciduous, hold the endemic Red Sanders tree and India's second-largest mangroves, and shelter rare animals such as Jerdon's Courser and wild elephants.

**Why it is asked:** 'Red Sanders is endemic to AP', 'Jerdon's Courser only in Sri Lankamalleswara' and 'Koundinya has AP's only wild elephants' are high-frequency APPSC facts.

## The story

**Flora** means plant life; **fauna** means animal life. AP's most widespread forest type is **Southern tropical dry deciduous** — trees that shed their leaves in the dry season. **Teak and bamboo** grow in the Godavari and north-coastal forests.

The star plant is **Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus)**. 'Endemic' means it grows naturally nowhere else; Red Sanders is **endemic** to AP's southern Eastern Ghats (the **Seshachalam-Palakonda-Lankamalla** belt). Because its red wood is so valuable, it is heavily **smuggled** and is protected under CITES. Along the coast, salt-tolerant **mangroves** at **Coringa** form India's **second-largest** mangrove stretch after the Sundarbans.

The animals are just as special. **Jerdon's Courser** is a **critically endangered**, night-active bird found nowhere else on earth except **Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary** in Kadapa; thought extinct, it was dramatically **rediscovered in 1986**. **Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary** in Chittoor is AP's **only** home for wild Asian elephants, which wandered in from Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. The coast also hosts Indian Bison (Gaur), the Golden Gecko and nesting olive-ridley turtles.

## Picture it

| AP natural 'first' | What / where |
|---|---|
| Red Sanders | Endemic tree, southern Eastern Ghats |
| Coringa | India's 2nd-largest mangrove |
| Jerdon's Courser | Only in Sri Lankamalleswara WLS, Kadapa |
| Koundinya WLS | AP's only wild elephants |

The **mangroves** of the Godavari and Krishna estuaries belong to the **tidal (littoral) forest** type.

## Terms explained

- **Flora / fauna** — plant life / animal life.
- **Deciduous** — trees that drop their leaves in the dry season.
- **Endemic** — found naturally in one place only, and nowhere else.
- **Critically endangered** — at extremely high risk of extinction.
- **CITES** — the international treaty that controls trade in threatened species (it protects Red Sanders).

**Four protected areas and what marks each**

| Protected area | Distinguishing feature |
|---|---|
| Sri Venkateswara National Park | in the Seshachalam (Tirupati) hills; part of the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve |
| Papikonda National Park | in the Papi Hills along the Godavari river |
| Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary | a major breeding site of spot-billed pelicans |
| Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary | the elephant sanctuary of Chittoor district |

## Don't confuse

- **Red Sanders is NOT sandalwood** — sandalwood (Santalum album) is chiefly a Karnataka/Tamil Nadu tree; Red Sanders is the AP endemic.
- **Jerdon's Courser lives only in Sri Lankamalleswara (Kadapa)** — not in NSTR or Coringa.
- **Koundinya, not NSTR, has AP's wild elephants.**

## Remember it

AP's wildlife 'onlys': endemic tree **Red Sanders**, only-habitat bird **Jerdon's Courser**, only-elephants sanctuary **Koundinya**, 2nd mangrove **Coringa**.

## TL;DR

- Southern tropical dry deciduous is AP's most widespread forest type; teak and bamboo occur in Godavari/north-coastal forests.
- Red Sanders is endemic to AP's southern Eastern Ghats (Seshachalam-Palakonda-Lankamalla) and is CITES-protected.
- Coringa (Godavari estuary) is India's second-largest mangrove after the Sundarbans.
- Jerdon's Courser (rediscovered 1986) survives only in Sri Lankamalleswara WLS, Kadapa; Koundinya WLS has AP's only wild elephants.

Koundinya WLS (Chittoor) is AP's only sanctuary with wild Asian elephants; Nelapattu is a major pelican breeding site.

### AP Districts and Headquarters (28) and the State's Extent

**In one line**
Andhra Pradesh has **28** districts since 31 December 2025; exam items ask a district's headquarters, which region it belongs to, and when it was created.

**The story**
Residuary Andhra Pradesh came into being on **2 June 2014**. It extends roughly from **12°41'** N to **19°07'** N and 76°50' E to 84°45' E, covering about 1,62,970 km² (about **4.96**% of India). It borders Odisha (**north-east**), Chhattisgarh (north), Telangana (north-west), **Karnataka (west)** and Tamil Nadu (south). Until 2022 there were 13 districts — **9 coastal** and **4 Rayalaseema** (Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur, Chittoor). On 4 April 2022 thirteen more were carved out, broadly one per **Lok Sabha** constituency. On **31 December 2025** Polavaram (HQ **Rampachodavaram**, from Alluri Sitharama Raju) and Markapuram (from Prakasam) were added. **Madanapalle** is not a district — it is the **headquarters** of Annamayya. The 28 **zilla parishads** start on 25 September 2026.

items.body:
### AP Relief — Eastern Ghats Ranges, Peaks, Gorges, Caves and Hill Stations

**In one line**
AP's relief question asks which hill range lies in which district, and what landmark (peak, cave, gorge, hill station) it holds.

**The story**
From the sea inland, AP rises from a coastal plain that is **widest** in the Godavari–Krishna delta and narrow near Visakhapatnam, to the broken Eastern Ghats (averaging about **600 m**, cut by the Godavari and Krishna **gaps**), and finally to the Rayalaseema plateau — the south-eastern edge of the Deccan at about **300–600** m with granite tors and **Cuddapah** sediments. The crescent-shaped **Cuddapah basin** of **Proterozoic** quartzite, shale and limestone underlies Kadapa–Kurnool and is why that belt holds barytes, limestone and uranium.

| Range / landmark | District | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| **Madugula Konda** range | Alluri Sitharama Raju (Paderu agency) | Arma Konda (~1,680 m), highest in AP and the Eastern Ghats |
| **Ananthagiri** hills | Alluri Sitharama Raju | **Araku** valley, Borra Caves, coffee |
| **Papi** Kondalu | Polavaram / Eluru / ASR | Godavari **gorge**; Papikonda NP |
| **Kondapalli** hills | NTR | Krishna gap; Kondapalli **toys** (GI) |
| **Nallamala** | Nandyal, Kurnool, Prakasam, Palnadu | between Krishna and Penner; **Srisailam**, NSTR, Chenchus |
| **Erramala** | Kurnool, Nandyal | west of the Nallamala; **Belum** Caves nearby |
| **Velikonda** | **Nellore**–Prakasam | eastern granite ridge; red sanders |
| **Palakonda** | YSR **Kadapa** | red sanders belt |
| **Lankamalla** | YSR Kadapa | Sri Lankamalleswara WLS (Jerdon's courser) |
| **Seshachalam** | Tirupati, YSR Kadapa | **Tirumala** temple; biosphere reserve, Talakona |
| **Horsley Hills** | Annamayya | ~1,265 m hill station, "**Ooty of Andhra**" |
| **Lambasingi** | Alluri Sitharama Raju | "**Kashmir of Andhra** Pradesh" — frost, sub-zero nights |
| **Gandikota** gorge | YSR Kadapa | Penner gorge, "**Grand Canyon** of India" |
| **Borra** Caves | Alluri Sitharama Raju | limestone (karst) caves of the **Gosthani**; stalactites; 1807 |
| **Belum** Caves | Nandyal | ~3.2 km; **second-longest** natural caves of the subcontinent; Patalaganga |
| **Yaganti** | Nandyal | Erramala caves and temple |
| **Dolphin's Nose** | Visakhapatnam | headland sheltering the harbour |
| **Maredumilli** | Godavari agency | forest eco-tourism |

**Don't confuse**
Arma Konda (Madugula Konda range) is AP's highest peak; Horsley Hills is the "Ooty of Andhra"; Lambasingi is the "Kashmir of Andhra". Borra Caves = Ananthagiri (north); Belum Caves = Nandyal (Rayalaseema). Gandikota = Penner gorge; Papi Kondalu = Godavari gorge.

**TL;DR**
- North: Madugula Konda (Arma Konda), Ananthagiri (Araku, Borra), Papi Kondalu (Godavari gorge).
- Centre/south: Nallamala (Srisailam), Erramala (Belum), Velikonda, Palakonda, Lankamalla, Seshachalam (Tirumala).
- Hill stations: Araku, Horsley Hills (Ooty of Andhra), Lambasingi (Kashmir of Andhra); Gandikota = Grand Canyon of India.
keyPoints: Arma Konda in the Madugula Konda range is the highest peak of AP and of the Eastern Ghats.
The Nallamala hills hold Srisailam and the Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam Tiger Reserve; the Seshachalam hills hold Tirumala.
Borra Caves (Ananthagiri hills, Gosthani river) are limestone caves; Belum Caves (Nandyal) are the second-longest in the subcontinent.
Horsley Hills is the "Ooty of Andhra"; Lambasingi the "Kashmir of Andhra Pradesh".
Gandikota gorge on the Penner is called the "Grand Canyon of India".

items.title: Rivers of AP in Detail — Deltas, Tributaries and Mouths
items.body:
### Rivers of AP in Detail — Deltas, Tributaries and Mouths

**In one line**
AP's **40 rivers** all run east; exam items ask where a tributary joins, where a river meets the sea, and which delta lies between which branches.

**The story**
The Godavari enters AP through the Papi Kondalu gorge and is barraged at **Dowleswaram** (Rajamahendravaram); below it the Gautami (east) and Vasishta (west) branches enclose **Konaseema**. **Yanam**, a **Puducherry** enclave, sits on the Gautami; the Vasishta reaches the sea at **Antarvedi**. The Krishna crosses Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar, is barraged at Vijayawada and reaches the sea near **Hamsaladeevi**, enclosing **Diviseema**. The **Penna** (Penner) crosses Anantapur, Kadapa (Gandikota) and Nellore and enters the sea near **Utukur**; its tributaries are the **Jayamangali**, Kunderu, Sagileru, Chitravathi, Papagni and **Cheyyeru**. Water shares were fixed by tribunals: the **Bachawat** KWDT-I (1976) and KWDT-II for the Krishna, and the Vamsadhara tribunal (2010) for the **Neradi** barrage dispute with Odisha.

| River | Key fact |
|---|---|
| **Sabari** | Kolab in Odisha; joins the Godavari near **Kunavaram** |
| **Sileru** | upper **Machkund**; Machkund, Upper and Lower Sileru (Donkarayi) hydel |
| **Tungabhadra** | joins the Krishna near **Sangameswaram** (submerged in Srisailam) |
| **Munneru**, **Paleru** | left-bank Krishna tributaries near Vijayawada |
| **Budameru** | stream of the 2024 **Vijayawada** floods, draining to Kolleru |
| **Chitravathi** | from Karnataka; joins the Penna near Gandikota |
| **Papagni** | from Karnataka; joins the Penna near **Kamalapuram** |
| **Kunderu** (Kundu) | drains the **Nandyal** valley to the Penna |
| **Vamsadhara** | from Odisha; mouth at **Kalingapatnam** |
| **Nagavali** (**Langulya**) | from Odisha; mouth near Srikakulam |
| **Gundlakamma** | Nallamala → **Prakasam** (Ongole) |
| **Swarnamukhi** | past **Srikalahasti** |
| **Gosthani** | Borra Caves → **Bheemunipatnam** |
| **Yeleru** | reservoir supplying Visakhapatnam steel |
| **Sarada**, Varaha | short Anakapalli rivers |

**Don't confuse**
Gautami = eastern Godavari branch (Yanam); Vasishta = western (Antarvedi). Vamsadhara mouth = Kalingapatnam; Nagavali mouth = near Srikakulam. Chitravathi and Papagni both join the Penna in Kadapa.

**TL;DR**
- Godavari: Dowleswaram → Gautami/Vasishta, Konaseema, Yanam; Sabari and Sileru join from the north.
- Krishna: Sangameswaram (Tungabhadra), Munneru/Paleru, mouth near Hamsaladeevi.
- Penna: Jayamangali, Kunderu, Chitravathi, Papagni, Cheyyeru, mouth near Utukur; north-coast Vamsadhara and Nagavali from Odisha.
keyPoints: Below Dowleswaram the Godavari splits into the Gautami and Vasishta; Konaseema lies between them and Yanam is on the Gautami.
The Sabari joins the Godavari near Kunavaram; the Sileru (upper Machkund) carries the Machkund and Sileru hydel stations.
The Tungabhadra joins the Krishna near Sangameswaram; the Krishna meets the sea near Hamsaladeevi.
Penna tributaries include the Chitravathi, Papagni, Kunderu and Cheyyeru.
The Vamsadhara reaches the sea at Kalingapatnam; the Nagavali (Langulya) near Srikakulam.

items.title: AP Irrigation, River-link and Hydel Projects
items.body:
### AP Irrigation, River-link and Hydel Projects

**In one line**
AP stores its east-flowing rivers in deltas and lifts them uphill to dry Rayalaseema; match questions pair a project with its river and its purpose.

**The story**
The deltas were tamed in the 19th century: **Sir Arthur Cotton** built the **Dowleswaram** anicut on the Godavari (1852) and the Krishna anicut at Vijayawada (1855), replaced by the **Prakasam Barrage** in **1957**. The private Madras Irrigation Company dug the **KC Canal** in the 1860s. After independence came Nagarjuna Sagar, Srisailam and the Tungabhadra **High Level** and **Low Level** canals. Since the 1980s AP has built lift and diversion schemes to carry Krishna water to Rayalaseema and Chennai. **Polavaram** (**Indira Sagar**) is the flagship, declared a national project under **Section 90** of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

| Project | River / source | Purpose / note |
|---|---|---|
| **Sir Arthur Cotton** Barrage (**Dowleswaram**) | Godavari | anicut 1852; Godavari delta irrigation |
| **Prakasam Barrage** | Krishna | Vijayawada; 1957 (Cotton's anicut 1855) |
| **Polavaram** (**Indira Sagar**) | Godavari | national project, **Section 90** of AP Reorganisation Act 2014 |
| **Pattiseema** lift | Godavari → Krishna | 2015–16; first **Godavari–Krishna** link |
| **Pulichintala** | Krishna | Palnadu–Telangana border |
| **Telugu Ganga** | Krishna (Srisailam) → **Kandaleru** → Chennai | 1983; drinking water to Chennai |
| **Handri-Neeva** | Krishna (Srisailam backwater) | lift to Kurnool, **Anantapur**, Kadapa, Chittoor |
| **Galeru-Nagari** | Krishna → **Gandikota** reservoir | Kadapa–Chittoor |
| **Veligonda** (Pula Subbaiah) | Krishna (Srisailam) | Nallamala **tunnel** to Markapuram–Prakasam |
| **KC Canal** (Kurnool–Cuddapah) | Tungabhadra (Sunkesula) | 1860s, **Madras Irrigation** Company |
| SRBC / **Pothireddypadu** | Krishna (Srisailam) | Rayalaseema diversion |
| **Thotapalli** | **Nagavali** | north-coastal irrigation |
| **Gotta** barrage | **Vamsadhara** | Srikakulam |
| **Machkund** hydel | Machkund (upper Sileru) | joint AP–**Odisha**, 1955; Duduma falls |
| **Somasila** | Penna | Nellore; linked to Kandaleru |
| Tungabhadra **High Level** / **Low Level** Canals | Tungabhadra | Anantapur, Kurnool |
| Srisailam | Krishna | hydel; left/right bank **power houses** |

**Don't confuse**
Telugu Ganga = drinking water to CHENNAI (via Kandaleru); Handri-Neeva and Galeru-Nagari = Rayalaseema lifts; Veligonda = Nallamala tunnel to Prakasam. Pattiseema = first Godavari–Krishna link. Machkund = AP–Odisha joint hydel.

**TL;DR**
- Cotton: Dowleswaram 1852, Krishna anicut 1855 → Prakasam Barrage 1957; KC Canal 1860s.
- Rayalaseema lifts: Handri-Neeva, Galeru-Nagari (Gandikota), SRBC/Pothireddypadu, Veligonda tunnel.
- Telugu Ganga to Chennai; Pattiseema links Godavari to Krishna; Thotapalli (Nagavali), Gotta (Vamsadhara), Machkund (AP–Odisha).
keyPoints: Sir Arthur Cotton built the Dowleswaram anicut on the Godavari in 1852; the Prakasam Barrage at Vijayawada dates from 1957.
Polavaram (Indira Sagar) is a national project under Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
The Pattiseema lift (2015–16) was the first Godavari–Krishna link.
Telugu Ganga carries Krishna water via the Kandaleru reservoir to Chennai.
Thotapalli barrage is on the Nagavali, Gotta barrage on the Vamsadhara; Machkund is a joint AP–Odisha hydel project.

items.title: AP Lakes, Wetlands, Coast, Islands and Ports
items.body:
### AP Lakes, Wetlands, Coast, Islands and Ports

**In one line**
AP's wetlands and coast are tested through Kolleru, Pulicat, bird sanctuaries, sand spits and ports.

**The story**
**Kolleru** lies between the Godavari and Krishna deltas (Eluru–Krishna districts); it became a wildlife sanctuary in **1999** and a Ramsar site in **2002**. It is fed by the Budameru and **Tammileru** and drains through the **Upputeru** to the sea. Aquaculture encroachment led to **Operation Kolleru** (2006). **Atapaka** bird sanctuary is part of it. **Pulicat** lagoon (Tirupati district and Tamil Nadu) is famous for flamingos and hosts the **Flamingo Festival**; **Sriharikota** island between the lagoon and the sea houses the **Satish Dhawan** Space Centre. The coast runs from **Ichchapuram** (Srikakulam) to Pulicat. Traditionally measured at 974 km (longest on the east coast), the 2024 re-measurement put India's coastline at **11,098**.81 km and AP's at about **1,053** km — third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu. AP has about **1,140** km² of coastal wetlands. The 2004 tsunami hit the Krishna–Prakasam coast (**Nizampatnam**).

| Wetland / coastal feature / port | Fact |
|---|---|
| **Nelapattu** | spot-billed **pelican** breeding site (Tirupati district) |
| **Uppalapadu** | pelicans and painted storks near Guntur |
| **Telineelapuram**, Telukunchi | Srikakulam heronries |
| **Kondakarla** Ava | freshwater lake, Anakapalli |
| **Hope Island** | Godavari sand spit sheltering **Kakinada** Bay |
| **Gangavaram** | one of India's **deepest** ports (~21 m) |
| **Krishnapatnam** | deep-water port, **Nellore** |
| **Kakinada** | **anchorage** + deep-water port; KG gas hub |
| **Ramayapatnam**, Machilipatnam, **Mulapeta** | greenfield ports under construction |

**Don't confuse**
Kolleru = freshwater, Ramsar 2002; Pulicat = brackish, not Ramsar-listed. 974 km is the traditional coastline; 1,053 km (2024 re-measurement) ranks AP third.

**TL;DR**
- Kolleru: WLS 1999, Ramsar 2002; Tammileru in, Upputeru out; Operation Kolleru 2006.
- Pulicat: flamingos, Flamingo Festival, Sriharikota barrier; Nelapattu pelicans.
- Coast 974 km (old) / ~1,053 km (2024); Gangavaram deepest; Hope Island shelters Kakinada.
keyPoints: Kolleru became a wildlife sanctuary in 1999 and a Ramsar site in 2002; it drains to the sea through the Upputeru.
Sriharikota island, between Pulicat lagoon and the sea, hosts the Satish Dhawan Space Centre.
Nelapattu is a spot-billed pelican breeding site; Pulicat hosts the Flamingo Festival.
The 2024 re-measurement put AP's coastline at about 1,053 km (third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu); India's at 11,098.81 km.
Hope Island, a Godavari sand spit, shelters Kakinada Bay; Gangavaram is one of India's deepest ports.

items.title: AP Climate Extremes and the Cyclone Record
items.body:
### AP Climate Extremes and the Cyclone Record

**In one line**
AP's climate questions ask for the driest/wettest/hottest places and for which cyclone hit which part of the coast in which year.

**The story**
Rain falls mainly from the SW monsoon, but the NE monsoon (Oct–Dec) is the main season for south-coastal **Nellore**–Tirupati and southern Rayalaseema. The north-coastal **agency** (Srikakulam, Alluri Sitharama Raju) is the wettest; **Anantapuramu** (about 550 mm) is the driest — often called India's second-driest district after **Jaisalmer**. **Rentachintala** (Palnadu) is cited as the hottest place. Most of AP lies in seismic **zones II and III**. The Godavari's record flood at Dowleswaram came in August **1986**. Cyclones peak in **October–December**, with a smaller May peak.

| Cyclone | When | Where / impact |
|---|---|---|
| **Diviseema** cyclone | Nov **1977** | Krishna delta; ~10,000 deaths by storm surge |
| Konaseema cyclone | Nov **1996** | landfall near **Kakinada** |
| **Laila** | May **2010** | near Bapatla |
| **Hudhud** | Oct **2014** | Visakhapatnam |
| **Titli** | Oct 2018 | **Srikakulam**/Odisha border (Palasa) |
| **Phethai** | Dec 2018 | near **Katrenikona** |
| **Gulab** | Sept 2021 | near **Kalingapatnam** |
| **Michaung** | 5 Dec 2023 | near **Bapatla** |
| **Montha** | 28 Oct 2025 | near **Narsapur**; ~87,000 ha crops |

**Don't confuse**
Hudhud (2014) = Visakhapatnam; Titli (2018) = Srikakulam; Michaung (2023) = Bapatla; Montha (2025) = Narsapur; Diviseema (1977) = Krishna delta surge.

**TL;DR**
- Driest Anantapur (~550 mm, second to Jaisalmer); wettest north-coastal agency; hottest Rentachintala.
- Cyclones: Diviseema 1977, Kakinada 1996, Laila 2010, Hudhud 2014, Titli 2018, Phethai 2018, Gulab 2021, Michaung 2023, Montha 2025.
keyPoints: Anantapuramu is AP's driest district, often called India's second-driest after Jaisalmer.
The NE monsoon is the main rain season for south-coastal AP (Nellore–Tirupati).
The 1977 Diviseema cyclone killed about 10,000 people in the Krishna delta.
Hudhud (2014) hit Visakhapatnam; Michaung (2023) Bapatla; Montha (28 Oct 2025) Narsapur.

items.title: Minerals of AP and Where They Occur
items.body:
### Minerals of AP and Where They Occur

**In one line**
AP is "**Ratna Garbha**"; a mineral question pairs a place (often in the Cuddapah basin or on the coast) with its mineral.

**The story**
Most of AP's minerals come from three settings: the Proterozoic Cuddapah basin of Kadapa–Kurnool (barytes, limestone, uranium, asbestos, dolomite and **steatite**), the old Dharwar schist and granite belts (gold, diamonds, mica, manganese), and the young coast and KG basin (beach sands, oil and gas). Residuary AP has little coal — only **Chintalapudi** (Eluru); the Godavari valley coalfield (**Singareni**) went to Telangana in 2014.

| Mineral | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Barytes** | **Mangampet** (Kadapa region) | one of the world's largest; AP leads India |
| **Uranium** | **Tummalapalle** (YSR Kadapa) | UCIL mine and mill |
| **Black Galaxy** granite | **Chimakurthy** (Prakasam) | export granite |
| Limestone | Kadapa, Kurnool, Palnadu, Anantapur | **cement** belt — **Yerraguntla**, Dachepalli |
| Bauxite | Alluri Sitharama Raju agency | **Chintapalli**, **Jerrela**, Araku (contentious mining) |
| Beach sands | Srikakulam–Bheemunipatnam–Kakinada coast | **ilmenite**, rutile, garnet, **monazite** (thorium), zircon |
| Mica | Nellore–**Gudur** belt | one of India's main **mica** belts |
| Diamonds | **Vajrakarur** (Anantapur); **Kollur** (Krishna gravels) | kimberlite pipes; Golconda diamonds, Koh-i-noor |
| Gold | **Ramagiri**; **Chigargunta**–Bisanatham | Dharwar schist belts |
| Asbestos | Brahmanapalli, **Pulivendula** | chrysotile |
| **Manganese** | **Garbham** (Vizianagaram), Srikakulam |  |
| Oil and natural gas | Krishna–Godavari basin | **Ravva** field; **KG-D6** (2002) |

**Don't confuse**
Mangampet = barytes; Tummalapalle = uranium (both Kadapa). Chimakurthy = black granite. Vajrakarur = diamonds; Ramagiri = gold. Singareni coal is in Telangana, not AP.

**TL;DR**
- Kadapa belt: barytes (Mangampet), uranium (Tummalapalle), asbestos (Pulivendula), limestone (Yerraguntla).
- Others: granite (Chimakurthy), mica (Gudur), diamonds (Vajrakarur, Kollur), gold (Ramagiri, Chigargunta), manganese (Garbham), bauxite (Jerrela–Chintapalli).
- Coast/KG: beach sands (ilmenite, monazite); Ravva and KG-D6 oil–gas.
keyPoints: Mangampet holds one of the world's largest barytes deposits; Tummalapalle (Kadapa) holds major uranium reserves.
Chimakurthy (Prakasam) is known for "Black Galaxy" granite; Gudur (Nellore) for mica.
Vajrakarur (Anantapur) has diamond-bearing kimberlite pipes; Ramagiri has gold.
Bauxite occurs in the Jerrela–Chintapalli agency; beach sands carry ilmenite and monazite.
The KG basin has the Ravva oil field and the KG-D6 gas discovery.

items.title: AP Forest Types, Protected Areas and State Symbols
items.body:
### AP Forest Types, Protected Areas and State Symbols

**In one line**
AP protected-area questions pair a sanctuary with its district and its star species; forest questions ask the types and where red sanders grows.

**The story**
AP's forests are mainly southern tropical dry deciduous, with moist deciduous forest in the north-coastal agency, tropical **thorn** scrub in Rayalaseema, tropical **dry evergreen** forest on the south coast and mangroves in the estuaries. **Alluri Sitharama Raju** has the largest forest cover (ISFR 2023). Red sanders grows in the Seshachalam, Lankamalla, Palakonda and **Veligonda** hills. NSTR was declared a tiger reserve in **1983**; it spreads over Nandyal, Prakasam, Palnadu, Kurnool and Guntur, and its Telangana part became **Amrabad** TR. Rajiv Gandhi (**Rameswaram**) NP in Kadapa is AP's **smallest** park. The **golden gecko** is endemic to the Tirumala hills, and **olive ridley** turtles nest on the coast. Big zoos: **Indira Gandhi Zoological** Park (Visakhapatnam) and Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park (Tirupati).

| Sanctuary / symbol | District / name | Known for |
|---|---|---|
| **Coringa** WLS | Kakinada | **1978**; Godavari-estuary mangroves |
| **Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary** | Krishna, Bapatla | 1989; **Krishna-estuary** mangroves, fishing cat |
| **Rollapadu** WLS | Nandyal (Kurnool) | great Indian bustard, lesser **florican** |
| Sri **Lankamalleswara** WLS | YSR Kadapa | **Jerdon**'s courser |
| **Koundinya** WLS | Chittoor | wild elephants; **Rayala** Elephant Reserve |
| **Gundla Brahmeswaram** WLS | Nandyal–Prakasam | Nallamala, next to NSTR |
| Sri **Penusila** Narasimha WLS | Nellore | Velikonda hills |
| **Kambalakonda** WLS | Visakhapatnam | urban hill forest |
| State animal | **blackbuck** (**Krishna Jinka**) |  |
| State bird | rose-ringed **parakeet** (**Rama Chiluka**), 2018 | replaced the Indian roller (now Telangana's) |
| State tree | **neem** (**Vepa**) |  |
| State flower | **jasmine** (**Malle**) |  |

**Don't confuse**
Coringa = Godavari mangroves; Krishna WLS = Krishna mangroves. Rollapadu = bustard/florican; Lankamalleswara = Jerdon's courser; Koundinya = elephants. State bird changed in 2018 to the rose-ringed parakeet (the Indian roller is Telangana's).

**TL;DR**
- Forest types: dry deciduous (dominant), moist deciduous, thorn, dry evergreen, mangrove.
- Sanctuaries: Coringa, Krishna, Rollapadu, Lankamalleswara, Koundinya, Gundla Brahmeswaram, Penusila, Kambalakonda.
- Symbols: blackbuck, rose-ringed parakeet, neem, jasmine.
keyPoints: AP's forests are mainly southern tropical dry deciduous, with thorn forest in Rayalaseema and dry evergreen forest on the south coast.
Coringa (1978) protects Godavari mangroves; Krishna WLS (1989) the Krishna-estuary mangroves.
Rollapadu protects the great Indian bustard and lesser florican; Koundinya is part of the Rayala Elephant Reserve.
NSTR became a tiger reserve in 1983; its Telangana part is now Amrabad Tiger Reserve.
AP state symbols: blackbuck (animal), rose-ringed parakeet (bird), neem (tree), jasmine (flower).

items.title: AP Waterfalls, Reservoir Names and Canals
items.body:
### AP Waterfalls, Reservoir Names and Canals

**In one line**
AP exam items ask the river or district of a waterfall, and the official names of big reservoirs and canals.

**The story**
AP's falls drop off the Eastern Ghats: the highest is **Talakona** (~**82** m) in Sri Venkateswara NP; **Ethipothala** on the **Chandravanka** near Nagarjuna Sagar has a crocodile breeding centre; **Katiki** tumbles near the Borra Caves; **Duduma** on the Machkund forms the AP–Odisha border. Many reservoirs carry a leader's name: Srisailam is **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** Sagar; Pulichintala is **K.L. Rao** Sagar; Polavaram is Indira Sagar. Nagarjuna Sagar's right canal is the **Jawahar** canal and its left canal the **Lal Bahadur** Shastri canal.

| Waterfall | District | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Talakona** | Tirupati (Sri Venkateswara NP) | highest fall in AP (~**82** m) |
| **Ethipothala** | Palnadu (near Nagarjuna Sagar) | **Chandravanka** stream; crocodile breeding centre |
| **Katiki** | Alluri Sitharama Raju | Gosthani, near Borra Caves |
| **Kailasakona** | Tirupati–Chittoor | near Puttur |
| **Ubbalamadugu** (**Tada**) | Tirupati | Siddulaiah Kona hills |
| **Rampa** | Polavaram district | near Rampachodavaram |
| **Duduma** | AP–Odisha border | Machkund river |

| Reservoir / canal | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** Sagar | Srisailam reservoir, Krishna |
| **Jawahar** canal / **Lal Bahadur** Shastri canal | Nagarjuna Sagar right / left canals |
| **K.L. Rao** Sagar | Pulichintala reservoir, Krishna |
| **Velugodu**; **Brahmamgari** Matham | Telugu Ganga balancing reservoirs |
| **Mylavaram**, Gandikota | Penna reservoirs, Kadapa |
| **Chitravathi Balancing** Reservoir | Anantapur–Sri Sathya Sai |
| **Raiwada**, **Thandava** | Anakapalli reservoirs |
| **Madduvalasa** | Vizianagaram |

**Don't confuse**
Talakona (Tirupati) is the highest fall in AP; Ethipothala is on the Chandravanka, not the Krishna mainstream. Jawahar = right canal; Lal Bahadur = left canal.

**TL;DR**
- Falls: Talakona (highest), Ethipothala, Katiki, Kailasakona, Tada, Rampa, Duduma.
- Names: Srisailam = Neelam Sanjiva Reddy Sagar; Pulichintala = K.L. Rao Sagar; NS right canal = Jawahar.
keyPoints: Talakona in Sri Venkateswara National Park is the highest waterfall in AP.
Ethipothala falls on the Chandravanka stream lies near Nagarjuna Sagar.
The Srisailam reservoir is named Neelam Sanjiva Reddy Sagar.
Nagarjuna Sagar's right canal is the Jawahar canal; its left canal the Lal Bahadur Shastri canal.

items.title: AP Agro-climatic Zones and Soil Distribution
items.body:
### AP Agro-climatic Zones and Soil Distribution

**In one line**
AP's six agro-climatic zones each pair a district group with a soil, a rainfall type and signature crops.

**The story**
Red soils (sandy and loamy) cover the largest share of AP, **followed by black** soils; alluvial soils line the deltas. Black soils dominate Krishna–Guntur–Prakasam and **western Kurnool**–Nandyal, growing cotton, chillies and **tobacco**. The Godavari–Krishna delta is the "**Rice Bowl**" of AP and Konaseema is famous for **coconut**. Coastal sandy and saline soils fringe the shore, with **problem saline** patches in Nellore and Krishna.

| Zone | Districts | Soil / crops |
|---|---|---|
| **North Coastal** | Srikakulam, **Vizianagaram**, Visakhapatnam plains | rice, sugarcane, mesta |
| **Godavari zone** | East & West Godavari (Konaseema, Eluru) | delta rice, coconut, oil palm |
| **Krishna zone** | Krishna, Guntur, parts of Prakasam | black soils; cotton, **chillies**, tobacco |
| **Southern zone** | Nellore, Chittoor, parts of Kadapa | NE-monsoon rain; rice, groundnut |
| Scarce Rainfall zone | Kurnool, Anantapur, parts of Kadapa/Prakasam | **groundnut**, millets |
| High Altitude & Tribal Areas | Eastern Ghats agency (ASR, Polavaram, Manyam) | **coffee**, pepper, millets |

**Don't confuse**
Krishna zone = black soils with chillies (Guntur) and tobacco; Scarce Rainfall zone = red soils with groundnut; Godavari zone = delta rice.

**TL;DR**
- Zones: North Coastal, Godavari, Krishna, Southern, Scarce Rainfall, High Altitude & Tribal.
- Red soils most widespread, then black; alluvial in deltas; Rice Bowl = Godavari–Krishna delta.
keyPoints: Red soils cover the largest share of AP, followed by black soils.
The Krishna zone (Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam) has black soils with cotton, chillies and tobacco.
The Scarce Rainfall zone (Kurnool, Anantapur) grows groundnut and millets.
The Godavari–Krishna delta is the Rice Bowl of AP.

items.title: For Mains — Physical Geography of Andhra Pradesh
items.body:
**In one line:** For Mains (Paper-II, General Studies - geography of India and AP), physical geography is asked not as a list of facts but as a resource-and-hazard story: how AP's relief, rivers, minerals and forests shape its development and its vulnerabilities.

This note serves syllabus clauses **M2-11** (physical features and resources of India and AP) and **M2-14** (fauna and floral geography). Examiners reward answers that convert the Prelims facts into analysis — linking relief to soils to agriculture, and resources to conservation conflict.

## Dimensions Mains asks

| Dimension | What to write |
|---|---|
| Features | Three belts (coastal plains, Eastern Ghats, Rayalaseema plateau); east-flowing rivers; 974 km coast |
| Significance | Delta rice-bowl, Ratna Garbha minerals, ports, second-largest mangroves |
| Problems | Coast-versus-Rayalaseema water imbalance, cyclones and floods, Red Sanders smuggling, mining in tribal forests |
| Way forward | Inter-basin transfers, mangrove shelter-belts, eco-sensitive-zone rules, community (Chenchu) conservation |

## Data points to quote

- ISFR 2023: forest cover 18.46% (30,084.96 sq km) versus recorded forest area 22.84% (37,221.11 sq km).
- Coastline about 974 km (longest on India's east coast); Visakhapatnam the only major port.
- Mangampeta (Kadapa) barytes among the world's largest; Tummalapalli uranium among the largest reserves.
- Cyclone Hudhud (2014) at Visakhapatnam; Michaung (2023) and Montha (2025) hit the coast — use for disaster-management angle.
- Polavaram National Project (Godavari); Handri-Neeva lift to drought-prone Rayalaseema.

## AP angle

Stress the sharp internal contrast: a water-rich, cyclone-exposed delta coast against a chronically drought-hit Rayalaseema. This single tension explains AP's lift-irrigation push, its disaster-management stakes, and the clash between mining or aquaculture and fragile Eastern-Ghats and estuarine ecosystems.

## Use in answers

- Example: cite Hudhud (2014) and Montha (2025) when arguing for mangrove shelter-belts and early-warning systems.
- Quote: AP as 'Ratna Garbha' (womb of gems) to open a resources answer.
- Diagram idea: a simple west-to-east cross-section (Rayalaseema plateau - Eastern Ghats - coastal delta - Bay of Bengal) instantly shows relief, soils and the water gradient.
keyPoints: Mains (Paper-II, clauses M2-11 and M2-14) asks physical geography as a resource-and-hazard story, not a fact list.
Frame answers along features, significance, problems and way forward; link relief to soils to agriculture.
Quote ISFR 2023 (cover 18.46% versus recorded 22.84%), 974 km coast, Mangampeta barytes, Tummalapalli uranium, Polavaram.
Core AP angle: water-rich cyclone-prone delta coast versus drought-prone Rayalaseema, driving lift irrigation and disaster management.
Use recent cyclones (Hudhud 2014, Montha 2025), the 'Ratna Garbha' quote, and a west-to-east cross-section diagram.
